agent_rule: Anything acting as an agent has a PKI key and either write access to git (L4) or the ability to create and consume vaults (L2). A chat-only helper (L0) is a tool used by a person, not an agent.

formula.place: the cheapest (r, m) such that io(r) >= io(t), loop(r) contains loop(t), identity(r) >= identity(t), trust(r, m) >= data(t), capability(m) >= judgement(t), reach(r) contains network(t), latency(r, m) <= time(t), oversight(r) >= oversight(t), modes(r, m) contains state(t)
formula.calls: inside an agent, model(c) = the cheapest tier whose capability >= difficulty(c), through admin/tools/llm.mjs; M3 when the data is private or the volume large and latency does not matter

rules: A task's state(t) is the longest-lived state it needs: none (S0), a conversation (S1), or memory across runs (S2).
State we must keep (decisions, evidence, anything the swarm reads later) lives in our record: git, a vault, a status file. A chat session (S1) is never the only copy.
A chat session is the cheapest way to use a frontier model with a person in the loop; an agent loop is the only one that can act on our repository.
Dinis's word in an agent's own session is a chat-session input to that agent (S1 into S2): the agent records it in a file so it outlives the session (briefs/, its status).
